- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias in next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model overreacts; adjust forecast to align with recent low range.
- When sentiment is low (≤ 0.33) and price drops, model underreacts; increase downward forecast sensitivity.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply upward bias for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model fails to capture volatility; smooth forecast curve to match sentiment swing amplitude.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 15d average, adjust forecast to align with 15d moving average unless sentiment strongly supports trend.
